precepts.text: Many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers, who were ancient men that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; and many shouted aloud for joy: so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; and the noise was heard afar off.
precepts.point: Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? Remember, they were in Babylon for 70 years; Cyrus came in at the end of the 70 years, then Darius. So the question is, who is still alive that saw the temple that Solomon built? When they rebuilt the temple, it did not look half as good as what Solomon had built.
precepts.why:
“Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?” They had been in Babylon for 70 years; Cyrus came in at the end of the 70 years, then Darius. So the question is, who is still alive that saw the temple Solomon built? When they rebuilt the temple, it did not look half as good as what Solomon had built.

Ezra shows those men: “But many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers, who were ancient men, that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice”. Old men who had seen Solomon's temple cried with a loud voice.

“and many shouted aloud for joy: So that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people: for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard afar off.” The young rejoiced at a foundation; the ancient men wept, because in their eyes it was as nothing in comparison to the first glory.

That house Zerubbabel rebuilt was completed around 515 BC, but it did not compare. That is why, in the time of Rome, Herod the Edomite would come and renovate it to make it look good.

precepts.text: When the seventh month was come, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Ezra 3:1 says the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem. Imagine how much could be done with one mind, one spirit and one judgment.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Paul beseeches the brethren “that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” When did we all speak the same thing? In the time of King David and King Solomon, when we ruled the nations. At one time we were unified, and we put the heathen, the other nations, in subjection. Are we unified today?

Ezra shows what that looks like: “And when the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.” As one man. Think about it on the Sabbath day: we come to hear the word of the Lord, and they gathered themselves together as one man.

Imagine us being perfectly joined together as one man. Imagine how much we could get done if we thought as one man, with the same mind, the same spirit and the same judgment. That is called unity.

It is the same unity Paul calls for in Ephesians 4: “Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace”, “Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man”. That perfect man is the one man. Brothers are going to offend brothers and sisters are going to offend sisters; get over it. There are bigger things to worry about than your feelings. Keep the unity no matter what, for the perfecting of the saints.

points: In the seventh month the children of Israel gather as one man to Jerusalem. The seventh month marks the Feast of Tabernacles and the day of atonement, so knowing the month reveals what they were doing.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: They set the altar on its bases despite fear of the surrounding peoples and offer burnt offerings morning and evening.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: They keep the Feast of Tabernacles and the daily offerings, but the foundation of the temple was not yet laid.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: They give money to the masons and carpenters, and meat, drink, and oil to the men of Zidon and Tyre to bring cedars from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the grant of Cyrus.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: In the second year of their coming, Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the remnant of their brethren the priests and Levites appoint the Levites from twenty years old and upward to set forward the work.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: The remnant here shows Judah, Benjamin, and Levi with those who had remained. Jeshua and his sons and brethren stand together to oversee the workmen.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: When the builders lay the foundation, the priests stand in their apparel with trumpets and the Levites with cymbals to praise the Lord after the ordinance of David.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: They sing together, praising and giving thanks, because the Most High is good and his mercy endures forever toward Israel, and all the people shout with a great shout.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: Many of the ancient priests and Levites who had seen the first house weep with a loud voice, while many shout aloud for joy.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: The people had endured Babylon tearing down Jerusalem, and now seeing the foundation raised again the noise of joy and weeping could not be discerned apart and was heard far off.
